summary: I lead and help build modern QA teams that keep up with the rapid pace of software development and the rise of AI.

I focus on QA leadership, quality strategy, and AI-driven testing. I enjoy exploring ways to use agent-based approaches and automation to eliminate repetitive QA work and move quality as close as possible to the start of the development process — ideally already during client communication and solution design.

I see QA as a partner to product and engineering, not a final gatekeeper. Automation and AI should handle execution and routine validation, while QA focuses on risk, overall quality, and continuous improvement across teams and products.

Although I primarily work in a leadership role, I stay hands-on where it adds value. I work with Playwright and TypeScript/JavaScript, focus on performance and load testing using k6, and have experience with CI/CD, DevOps practices, and Azure cloud environments. This allows me to connect QA strategy with real-world implementation and ensure that it does not remain just on paper, but actually works in practice.
I believe strong QA is built on clear ownership, trust within teams, data-driven decisions, and smart use of automation and AI.

intro: Leading QA across projects at Etnetera Core, with responsibility for QA strategy, quality standards, test automation direction, and the development of performance testing practices.

Alongside building scalable QA processes, mentoring QA engineers, and aligning quality with product and engineering goals, I am increasingly focused on how AI can fundamentally reshape the role of QA within a modern software development lifecycle.

My goal is not simply to automate individual testing tasks, but to move QA toward an AI-native model where the tester mindset — critical thinking, risk discovery, dealing with uncertainty, and the ability to challenge systems — becomes the foundation for orchestrating and directing AI agents.

In this model, AI increasingly takes over routine and repeatable activities, while QA engineers evolve into roles focused on defining strategy, context, risks, quality boundaries, and validation principles — using AI as an execution layer capable of autonomously handling a significant share of testing work.

I see this as the future of QA: less time spent manually executing routine tasks, and more focus on quality as a system, where human testers use their mindset and judgment to guide intelligent, autonomous agents across the entire SDLC.
Designing and developing automations for new and existing projects using Playwright, with the goal of streamlining processes and accelerating delivery.

vision.title: How I work
vision.text: Tools matter, but in the end it's about people. A happy team with room to grow ships a better product than a team with perfect processes and bad morale. So I don't just set up processes. Mostly I make sure the team is a good place to work.

intro.title: When I close the laptop
intro.description: I work at a computer, but I clear my head outside. Mountains if I can, the sea if I can't. My best ideas still show up when I'm not thinking about work.

categories.name: Mountains

categories.name: Water and running

projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: Stuff I'm building around testing with AI. Plus a guesthouse in the mountains where I try AI with my own money.

items.name: QA Control Center
items.description: You give it a requirement and AI drafts acceptance criteria, test scenarios and ready-to-run Playwright tests. I built it because I'd seen plenty of generated tests that pass and check nothing. So instead of pass rate, it tracks how much you can trust each test.
items.extra: There are human gates between the steps. Nothing moves on until QA says yes.

items.name: QA Brain
items.tagline: One set of QA rules for people and agents.
items.description: A set of QA rules where every rule has its own ID. Agents in Claude Code and Copilot read them and cite them, the way a colleague would in a code review.
items.extra: When an agent says which rule a test breaks, nobody has to ask why.

items.name: k6 performance framework
items.tagline: Even a PM can order a load test.
items.description: A framework on top of k6. A product manager who's never seen a script can order a load test with it. They answer five questions, or leave it all to the AI configurator.
items.extra: At the end they get a report they can read without a translator.

items.name: QA Manual Copilot
items.tagline: An AI sidekick for manual testers.
items.description: A Chrome extension that sits next to a manual tester. It suggests what else to try and helps write up a finding.
items.extra: It has one rule it can't skip: no claim without evidence. Every finding needs a screenshot, a log or an exact step.

items.name: MTP generator
items.tagline: A Master Test Plan that comes out the same every time.
items.description: A Master Test Plan generator. Code builds the structure, scope and rules from the input data, so the same data gives you the same plan.
items.extra: AI is only allowed to write the prose, like the intro and the summary.
